title: Penalties for Changing Land Use Purpose Without Permission (2026)
desc: Building on agricultural or rice land without a land use purpose change is fined up to VND 200 million in communes, double in wards; the land must be restored.
summary: Fines for converting rice land, agricultural land, or non-agricultural land to residential or other uses without permission under Decree 123/2024/ND-CP, and the remedial measures.
body: p

Building a house or workshop, or filling in a pond or garden, before the land has been converted to residential land is a very common violation. Using land for another purpose without permission from a competent state authority is penalized under Articles 8 to 12 of Decree 123/2024/ND-CP.
h2
1. Converting rice land to residential land
p
Under Clause 3, Article 8, in a commune:
ul
Under 0.01 ha (under 100 m²): VND 20–30 million.
From 0.01 to under 0.03 ha: VND 30–50 million.
From 0.03 to under 0.05 ha: VND 50–100 million.
From 0.05 to under 0.1 ha: VND 100–150 million.
From 0.1 ha and above: VND 150–200 million.
p

Converting rice land to non-agricultural land other than residential land (for warehouses, workshops, yards, etc.) in a commune: from VND 3–5 million (under 0.05 ha) to VND 100–150 million (from 2 ha) (Clause 2, Article 8).
h2
2. Converting other agricultural land (garden, pond, perennial crops) to residential land
p
Agricultural land that is not rice land or forestry land converted to residential land in a commune (Clause 2, Article 10):
ul
Under 0.01 ha: VND 10–20 million.
From 0.01 to under 0.03 ha: VND 20–30 million.
From 0.03 to under 0.05 ha: VND 30–50 million.
From 0.05 to under 0.1 ha: VND 50–100 million; from 0.1 ha and above: VND 100–150 million.
p
Converting to non-agricultural land other than residential land: from VND 3–5 million (under 0.05 ha) to VND 100–150 million (from 2 ha) (Clause 1, Article 10).
h2
3. Converting non-agricultural land (production and business land, etc.) to residential land
p

Converting non-agricultural land other than residential land to residential land in a commune: from VND 10–20 million (under 0.02 ha) to VND 150–200 million (from 0.5 ha) (Clause 2, Article 12). Forest land converted to another purpose is penalized under Article 9.
h2
4. Double in wards, double for organizations
ul
Violations within the boundaries of a ward or township are fined 2 times the corresponding amount in a commune (Clause 4, Article 8, Clause 3, Article 10, Clause 5, Article 12).
The amounts above apply to individuals; organizations are fined 2 times as much (Clause 2, Article 5).
h2
5. Remedial measures
ul
Restoring the land to its original condition (demolishing structures and returning the land to agricultural condition), except in cases considered under Clause 3 of Article 139 of the Land Law.

Surrendering the unlawful gain, calculated as the difference in land use right value between the land type after and before the violation according to the land price list (Point a, Clause 2, Article 6).
p

A dossier to apply for a house construction permit must include lawful land documents (Article 55 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP), so it is advisable to complete the conversion to residential land first and only then apply for the permit; see Procedure for applying for a detached house construction permit 2026.
h2
6. The right way to do it
ol
Check the land use purpose stated on the land use right certificate (sổ đỏ) and the local land use plan.
Submit an application for a land use purpose change, wait for the approval decision, and pay land use fees (if any).
Register the change in land use purpose (Point e, Clause 1, Article 133 of the Land Law).
Only then apply for a construction permit and start building.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. The fines above are ranges; the specific amount depends on the circumstances. The procedure and the authority that permits a land use purpose change follow the current documents on two-level local government. Decree 123/2024/ND-CP is shown as partially no longer in force on the National Legal Portal; the articles cited here have not been found amended in our library. After the abolition of the district level, penalizing authority and the names of administrative units (wards, townships) may have been adjusted by documents on two-level local government that are not yet in our library; it is advisable to ask the commune- or ward-level People's Committee where the land is located.
